newsitem.title: JAPAN: Policy shouldn't overemphasise forex stability-BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Policy shouldn't overemphasise forex stability-BOJ.

text.p: Japan's monetary policy should not overemphasise the aim of achieving stability in foreign exchange rates, Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday.
Matsushita, speaking at a parliamentary committee meeting, also said monetary policy should not be relied on heavily to correct imbalances in the current account.
"The aim of achieving stability of foreign exchange rates or a correction of major international imbalances should not depend heavily on monetary policy," he said.
Matsushita said the BOJ should carry out monetary policy with the aim of achieving sustainable economic growth without inflation.
He said the BOJ would take steps pre-emptively to achieve this goal.

Matsushita was referring to the central bank's policy in the late 1980s, when it took an easy monetary stance for a prolonged period to correct the strength of the yen at that time and to reduce Japan's current account surplus.
Matsushita admitted that the policy was one factor which brought about the so-called "bubble" economy of inflated asset prices.
